record.context_brief: Ideal fluids with sources and sinks
record.original_question: For an ideal incompressible inviscid fluid in a fixed domain M whose boundary may contain sources and sinks, can one give a variational, preferably geodesic, formulation of the motion? What boundary data, exterior forces, or memory variables must be included so that the formulation covers examples such as a pipe with inflow and outflow?

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent collection of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics (2022/2023). No subsequent work providing a fully satisfactory variational/geodesic formulation of ideal incompressible flow in domains with boundary sources and sinks (covering examples such as a pipe with inflow and outflow) appears in the literature. Related developments on generalized flows on groupoids of multiphase diffeomorphisms exist but do not resolve the question. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems (arXiv)
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics, including variational/geodesic formulations for fluids with sources and sinks.
status_evidence.claim: The variational/geodesic formulation for ideal fluids with boundary sources and sinks is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of generalized fluid flows
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized flows, multiphase fluids and vortex sheets as geodesics on groupoids of multiphase diffeomorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Related geodesic formulations on groupoids exist but do not address the sources/sinks boundary setting.
